rationale: Direct neuroradiological and clinical analysis across the largest reported cohort of biallelic NOTCH3 variants (50 patients total: 26 biallelic loss-of-function and 24 biallelic cysteine-altering missense) confirms a distinct genotype-imaging dichotomy. Biallelic loss-of-function variants produce early-onset disease characterized by periatrial white matter volume loss mimicking periventricular leukomalacia (PVL) with sparing of the anterior temporal poles, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants produce severe CADASIL-like phenotypes with deep white matter hyperintensities without prominent volume loss.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants cause a neurodevelopmental leukovasculopathy characterized by childhood-onset stroke, spasticity, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants result in an early adult-onset CADASIL spectrum phenotype with deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: Three patients with biallelic cysteine-sparing loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants presented at 9-14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, and extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, cerebral atrophy, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microbleeds, and calcifications, while anterior temporal poles were conspicuously spared.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: MRI findings pointed at a small vessel disease, with extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, atrophy, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microbleeds, and microcalcifications. The anterior temporal lobes were spared. Bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 were found.

new_directions.question_text: How do quantitative volumetric MRI markers differentiate early-stage biallelic NOTCH3 LoF from perinatal hypoxic-ischemic PVL in term and preterm infants without a genetic diagnosis?
new_directions.rationale: Because biallelic NOTCH3 LoF white matter injury mimics PVL, defining objective volumetric, DTI, or regional sparing thresholds (e.g. absence of temporal lobe and external capsule involvement) will improve diagnostic specificity before exome sequencing results return.

new_directions.question_text: Does NOTCH3 extracellular domain (N3ECD) aggregate deposition in skin biopsy differentiate biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants from biallelic loss-of-function variants?
new_directions.rationale: Classic CADASIL and cysteine-involving variants typically exhibit granular osmiophilic material (GOM) and N3ECD accumulation in vascular smooth muscle cells, whereas complete LoF variants are predicted to lack N3ECD accumulation, offering a tissue-based biomarker.
